title: Where are you from?
goal: Say where you're from, your nationality, and your job; say which languages you speak; and recognize the *-em* / *-ą* endings that always appear after *jestem*.
bekal: answer *skąd jesteś?* with a country and a city
give your job with *jestem…* and the right ending for men and women
say which languages you speak with *mówię po…*

dialogs.title: Dialogue — W kuchni akademika
dialogs.intro: The shared kitchen in a student dorm, late afternoon. Ania is making tea; Budi comes in with a mug.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Jestem z Indonezji, z Dżakarty. A ty jesteś z Krakowa, prawda?
lines.id: I'm from Indonesia, from Jakarta. And you're from Kraków, right?
lines.literal: I-am from Indonesia, from Jakarta. and you are from Kraków, true?

lines.speaker: Ania:
lines.text: Tak. Mieszkam w Krakowie od urodzenia. Co robisz w Polsce?
lines.id: Yes. I've lived in Kraków since I was born. What are you doing in Poland?
lines.literal: yes. I-live in Kraków since birth. what you-do in Poland?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Studiuję informatykę. A ty? Kim jesteś z zawodu?
lines.id: I study computer science. And you? What do you do for a living?
lines.literal: I-study computer-science. and you? who you-are by profession?

lines.speaker: Ania:
lines.id: I'm a teacher. I teach English.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Naprawdę? Mój brat też jest nauczycielem.
lines.id: Really? My brother is a teacher too.
lines.literal: really? my brother also is teacher-man.

lines.speaker: Ania:
lines.text: Świetnie! A mówisz po polsku bardzo dobrze.
lines.id: Great! And your Polish is really good.
lines.literal: great! and you-speak in-Polish very well.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Dziękuję, ale mówię tylko trochę. Uczę się dwa miesiące.
lines.id: Thanks, but I only speak a little. I've been learning for two months.
lines.literal: thanks, but I-speak only a-little. I-teach self two months.

lines.speaker: Ania:
lines.id: Two months? I don't believe it!

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Mówię po angielsku, po indonezyjsku i trochę po polsku.
lines.id: I speak English, Indonesian, and a little Polish.
lines.literal: I-speak in-English, in-Indonesian and a-little in-Polish.

lines.speaker: Ania:
lines.text: To dużo. Ja mówię tylko po polsku i po angielsku.
lines.id: That's a lot. I only speak Polish and English.
lines.literal: that a-lot. I speak only in-Polish and in-English.

notes: **Skąd** means "where from" — one word. It has two partners: *gdzie?* (where) and *dokąd?* (where to). English can blur these ("where are you going?"), but Polish keeps the three directions strictly apart, and using the wrong one sounds odd right away.

**Country names change after z.** *Indonezja* becomes *z Indonezji*, *Polska* becomes *z Polski*, *Kraków* becomes *z Krakowa*. This ending is called *dopełniacz* and will be covered fully in Unit 14. For now, memorize your own country as one chunk: **z Indonezji**.

**Mieszkam w Krakowie** — note the ending *-ie*. The city name changes again, in a **different** way from after *z*. The rule comes in Unit 11; for now, two ready-made chunks are enough: *z Krakowa* (from Kraków), *w Krakowie* (in Kraków).

**Kim jesteś z zawodu?** literally means "who are you by profession". Polish asks about jobs with "who", not "what" — because it's asking about the person, not a thing. The short answer is just *jestem nauczycielem*.
**Nauczycielem or nauczycielką?** A job after *jestem* always takes the *narzędnik* form: men get the ending **-em**, women get **-ą**. See the grammar box below.

**Mówię po polsku**, not *mówię polski*. The language is treated here as a **manner**: literally "I speak in a Polish way". This *po …-sku* form never changes at all, so it's one of the easiest things in the whole course.

**Uczę się** (I learn) and **uczę** (I teach) differ by one small word. *Się* shows that the action comes back to yourself: teaching yourself = learning. Dropping *się* changes the meaning completely.
**Nie wierzę** — notice that *nie* always stands **right before** the verb, with no helper word like English "don't". Polish negates in the simplest way imaginable: put *nie* in front of the verb.

grammars.title: Jestem + narzędnik — jobs and nationalities
body: A rule that looks complicated but is really one sentence: after *jestem*, a noun that says **who you are** takes a special ending.
after: There are only two endings: **-em** for men, **-ą** for women. If the base word ends in *k* or *g*, the ending becomes **-iem** (*Polak → Polakiem*) — that *i* just softens the sound; it isn't a separate thing to memorize.
The same rule works for everyone: *on jest studentem*, *ona jest studentką*, *jesteśmy studentami*.
⚠️ **Names** don't follow this rule: *Jestem Budi*, not *Jestem Budim*. Only common nouns change — jobs, nationalities, roles.

grammars.title: Languages: po …-sku
body: To say which language is being used, Polish doesn't use a noun but an adverb form that never changes.
after: It's used with the three most common verbs: *mówić* (speak), *rozumieć* (understand), *czytać* (read). *Rozumiem po polsku* = I understand Polish.
There's a second form used for **learning** a language: *uczę się polskiego* (I'm learning Polish) — here the language becomes a noun and changes its ending. Just recognize it as one chunk for now.

blocks.text: Three columns per country, because Polish uses different words for the country, its people, and its language. Nationalities are always **capitalized**; languages are always **lowercase**.
A helpful pattern: the female form is almost always **the male form + -ka** (*Polak → Polka*, *Anglik → Angielka*). The same pattern works for jobs too.

blocks.title: Where you come from
items: *Mieszkam w Dżakarcie.* — I live in Jakarta.
*Urodziłem się w Bandungu.* (m) / *Urodziłam się…* (f) — I was born in Bandung.

blocks.text: All of these are used with *jestem* + the ending *-em* (m) or *-ą* (f).

⚠️ *programista*, *sprzedawca*, and *kierowca* end in *-a* like feminine words, but they are **masculine** — because they mean male people. Their ending in *narzędnik* is still *-ą*: *jestem programistą*. A sensible exception, and there are only a few of them.

blocks.title: If your job isn't on the list
items: *Pracuję w banku / w szkole / w restauracji.* — I work at a bank / a school / a restaurant.
*Pracuję w firmie IT.* — I work at an IT company.
*Jeszcze się uczę.* — I'm still at school.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the right *narzędnik* form (ending *-em* or *-ą*).
Match each country with its language. Write a full sentence: *Mieszkam w… i mówię po…*
Put the words in the right order.

answers: Skąd jesteś? — Jestem z Indonezji. — Mieszkam w Krakowie. — Jestem studentem. — Ona jest nauczycielką. — Mówię trochę po polsku.
